context.description: The graph walk finds no stuck state in the release-notes plan (owner ruling 4)

evidence.trustReason: Fresh-context review of packages/opencode/test/task/verify-spec-RM19.spec.ts (3 tests, 26 expect calls). My runs: a whole-file run at load average about 125 was cut by my 178 s command limit with no result; the timed walk test alone then failed once on the 60 s bound only (73.9 s at load about 120, a load effect, assertions after it not reached); its one re-run passed (walk 338 keys, 746 edges, 26.9 s, 18 expect calls); the totality and negative-control tests passed (filtered run); a final whole-file run with the project command passed 3 of 3, 26 expect calls, walk 34.1 s at load about 50. GIVEN the release-notes plan and the engine's progress alphabet: release-notes.spec through the real loader (6 tasks, 13 scenarios asserted); the machine is TaskMachine.machine(plan); TaskMachine.check returns the config unchanged (owner ruling 4 (b)); the events come from the real TaskAlphabet.alphabet and the key from TaskAlphabet.walkKey, both in src. WHEN every state reachable with the canonical interleaving is walked within 60 s: the port's getAdjacencyMap from TaskEngineXState.initial with only the first unit in document order that has facts (owner ruling 4 (a); the same strategy as the T1.10 graph test, test-side, not code under test), stopWhen done; elapsed asserted under 60000 ms; edges asserted under the hang guard (the port fails past limit), so the walk was complete. THEN no state that is not done lacks an event that changes its key: the stuck list (not done and no transition to another key) equals []. AND every visited snapshot has status active or done: the set of statuses equals exactly [active, done]. Non-vacuous: more than 100 keys; done states with outcomes budget_exhausted, done, failed and needs_human; every state with T1.1-T1.3 trusted and T1.4 budget_exhausted has T1.5 and T1 blocked; a negative control on example-cascade.spec with the blocked rows removed makes the same detector report stuck states, including T1.2 waiting. Note: the 60 s bound has about a 2x margin on this shared host and fails under heavy load; that is an environment risk, not an assertion gap.
